items.title: feat(amd): wvkbd on-screen keyboard, tied to Sunshine streams
items.body: Drew streams the laptop desktop to his phone via Sunshine/Moonlight and asked for a permanent on-screen keyboard that runs ONLY while he is connected via Sunshine — not at plain desktop login (his steering; an unconditional Hyprland autostart was in the first cut and was removed before this PR). Changes: - `home/common/default.nix`: install `pkgs.wvkbd` in home.packages. - `nixos/hosts/amd-sunshine.nix`: wire Sunshine `global_prep_cmd` (key verified present in the pinned Sunshine binary, 2026.914.233613; the module renders the JSON string verbatim into sunshine.conf via its keyValue format) to two scripts: - `sunshine-wvkbd-start` at stream start: pgrep guard, then `setsid -f wvkbd-mobintl -L 500` (detached, returns immediately — Sunshine waits for prep commands to exit before streaming). - `sunshine-wvkbd-stop` at stream stop: `pkill -x wvkbd-mobintl`. - `config/hypr/hyprland.lua`: SUPER+SHIFT+O re-shows the keyboard (SIGUSR2; launches it if not running). SUPER+SHIFT+K was already taken by a workspace-move bind, hence O. Verification: full `nixosConfigurations.amd` toplevel builds on amd from this branch (after #7816 repaired the fleet package build, which was broken on main and blocked any toplevel build). Post-merge: switch + live checks (profile path, generated sunshine.conf, prep do/undo simulation, Sunshine/opencode services). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: test(id): journal the fixture issuance in scheduling_actor (#2894 fallout)
items.body: ## What broke Two `id` lib tests failed deterministically on main: - `world::tests::schedule_tests::a_fire_the_program_refuses_stays_pending_in_the_journal` - `world::tests::schedule_tests::replay_reproduces_the_pending_and_fired_sets` Both panicked at `WorldCore::restore(...).unwrap()` with `journal event at sequence 1 uses participant 1 before it was issued`. This also failed the `id` lib test target inside `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.amd.config.system.build.toplevel`, blocking the merged wvkbd deploy (#7817). ## Root cause — the test fixture was wrong, not the validation The restore event-author validation for #2894 merged this morning (PR #4518, 2026-11-08 02:25 CST). It is behaving as designed. The `scheduling_actor` fixture mints its participant by calling `WorldCore::issue_capability` directly and never journals the `Issued` entry. Production issuance goes through `WorldActor::record_issued`, which persists the `Issued` entry at mint time — so a real journal always records issuance before any event authored by that participant (the replica tests journal issuance the same explicit way). The fixture produced a journal no live path can write; once restore learned to refuse such journals, the two tests that feed the fixture's raw journal to `restore` failed. The journal-gate change in #4535 only touched the version check and builder-install persistence and is not implicated. ## Fix `scheduling_actor` appends `core.issued_entry(ann.id)` to its recorded journal immediately after minting — the same entry the actor persists in production. The journal the tests restore is now one the real system could have written. No production code changes. The #2894 author validation is not weakened, no test is skipped or deleted, and no fixture state is special-cased in restore. ## Verification (laptop) - The two named tests pass; all 21 `schedule_tests` pass. - Full package run — `cargo test` in `pkgs/id` — green on every target: lib 2478 passed / 0 failed, id_core 329, bin 10, all integration targets (cli_integration 127, crash 18, world_dos 11, …), doc tests 14. Tests-only change, so no other package is affected. Unblocks the amd toplevel build on main and the #7817 wvkbd deploy waiting on it. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR?
